sections.title: How much does it cost?
sections.content: To ask a price, use the fixed question *Mennyibe kerül ...?* ("How much does ... cost?"). Learn *mennyibe kerül* as one block. The thing follows it with no ending. The answer is the thing plus the price, and Hungarian needs no word for "is": *A kenyér háromszáz forint.* You can put the amount into the question: *Mennyibe kerül egy kiló alma?*

sections.title: Cheap and expensive
sections.content: *Olcsó* (cheap) and *drága* (expensive) work like the adjectives you know: *A tej olcsó.* To set two things against each other, use *de*: *A tej olcsó, de a sajt drága.*

items.english: How much does the bread cost?
How much does a kilo of apples cost?
A kilo of apples is 400 forints.

items.spanish: A tej olcsó, de a sajt drága.
items.english: The milk is cheap, but the cheese is expensive.

sections.content: In unit 19 the food you buy took *-t*: *Kenyeret vásárolok.* In a price question nobody does anything to the food, so there is no *-t*: *Mennyibe kerül a kenyér?* It is the thing the price belongs to, not the thing you buy.
